history.period: Unknown; local tradition claims Mahabharata-era antiquity (UNVERIFIED)
history.summary: Zand Hanuman Temple is a rock-carved Hanuman shrine deep inside the Jambughoda Wildlife Sanctuary, about 6-10 km from Jambughoda village in Panchmahal district. Local tradition holds that the Pandavas worshipped here during their exile and left behind relics such as the Bhima Ghanti (bell) and Arjun Ka Kuwa (well) - all UNVERIFIED legend, no archaeological confirmation. The main murti is an approximately 18-foot Hanuman figure carved directly from the mountain rock. The seawatersports.com listing additionally mentions an 18th-century building tradition under a regional ruler, which conflicts with the Mahabharata-era legend (CONFLICT - verify). It is a popular picnic and forest destination as well as a place of worship.

name: Zand Hanuman Temple
town_description: Jambughoda is a small town in Panchmahal district, east-central Gujarat, and the gateway to the Jambughoda Wildlife Sanctuary. It lies in a forested, largely tribal belt about 75-87 km southeast of Vadodara and roughly 35-40 km from Godhra, the district headquarters. Visitors pass through it to reach forest temples such as Zand Hanuman and the Kada Dam.

travel.airport: Vadodara Airport, about 75-87 km away (verify); alternatively Ahmedabad, about 190 km
travel.road: Reachable by road via Jambughoda village; the last stretch runs through the wildlife sanctuary on a rough, partly unpaved forest road. No public transport reported - private vehicle required (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; reviewers recommend just after the monsoon (September onward)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours only; visitors advise going between about 8 AM and 5 PM (verify). Leave the forest before dark as there is no marked route.
